page.layout: One page of running text in the main column, with a short marginal note ("Præc.") beside the upper lines and a longer marginal note block in the right margin. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword at bottom left.

main_text.p: ptas fuisse. Itaq; recenter capienda sint, & quidem ex aquis puris, diligenterq; denudandaPræc., tum abjecto capite elixanda, inq; sartagine frigenda. aspersa farina, & tandem apio. Gula generosior piperis pollinè salubriores & delicatiores reddit. Cibum non sentientibus, quos graeci ἀτρόφως appellant, nec non tabidisTabidis ranæ utiles: nolunt hoc Italæ fœminæ, q ut bene curato & succoso sint corpore iis utuntur crebrius. utilissime sumuntur. Antiquitas adversus venena eas magnificavit. Ætius l.2. c.162. & l.13.c.5. Item Æginetá l. 7. prodiderunt, ranarum jus cum sale oleo, haustum mirificè illis prodesse, qui à venenatis reptilibus essent percussi. Plinius his suffragatur l.32.c.5. ubi leguntur sequentia. Fluviatiles rana, si carnes earum edantur, jusq; vel decoctum sorbeatur, prosunt contra leporem marinum & contra serpentes. Item ranarum marinarum ex vino & aceto decoctarum succus contra venena bibitur & contra rubetæ venenum. Est autem rubeta in vepribus tantum vivens rana plena venefitii.

Mira sunt, qua Plinius certatim à scriptoribus tradita de rubeta prodidit. Illatus sc.in populum silentium fieri. Offiento[?] quod sit in dextro latere, in aquam ferventem dejecto, refrigerari vas, nec postea fervere, nisi exemto. Inveniri autem id objecta rana formicis carnibusq; erosis. Et aliud esse in finistro latere, quo dejecto fervere videatur, apocynum vocari: eo cohiberi canum impetus, amore concitari, et jurgia additó in potionem: venerem adalligatum simulare.

page.notes: Scan is partly faded and the left edge is cut, so the first word of the page is a fragment (ptas, probably the end of a longer word). The reference signs before "Antiquitas", "Ætius" and "Item" are printed marks; I have not reproduced them. Doubtful readings: "pollinè" (accent unclear), "ἀτρόφως" (Greek ending uncertain), "Offiento" (word unclear), "Ægineta/Æginetá" (last letter cut), "jusq;" and "crebrius" (ending uncertain). The page number is read as 127 from a faded numeral. The catchword "Rur" is partly cut off at the bottom right.
